psy_UoG_1.text: 32. Which of the following Big Five personality dimensions is associated with traits such as good-natured, trusting, caring and helpful?
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Agreeableness captures warmth, trust, cooperation, and helpfulness. Neuroticism reflects emotional instability, and extraversion reflects sociability and energy. Introversion is not a separate Big Five dimension but the low end of extraversion.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 33. Which theory of emotion is demonstrated by this statement, "I label my laughing as anxiety since I am in the middle of giving a speech in class"
psy_UoG_1.explanation: The Schachter-Singer two-factor theory holds that emotion arises from physiological arousal plus a cognitive label based on the situation. Here the arousal is labeled as anxiety because of the speech context. James-Lange and Cannon-Bard do not include a cognitive labeling step.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 34. Abebe is rarely on time for anything, is constantly losing things in his messy office, and can't really be relied upon to remember to do anything important around the office. According to the Big Five trait theory, Abebe would rate very low in ____________.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Conscientiousness reflects organization, punctuality, dependability, and self-discipline, so Abebe's disorganization and unreliability indicate very low conscientiousness. The behaviors described do not concern curiosity, warmth toward others, or emotional instability.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 35. Bitania has a phobia of rats. The biological model of abnormality would probably say that she had:

options.text: A. A childhood trauma involving rats.
C. Too much activity in the fear center of her brain.
D. Learned to associate rats with fear.

psy_UoG_1.explanation: The biological model attributes abnormal behavior to brain structure, neurochemistry, or genetics, such as overactivity in the amygdala, the brain's fear center. Childhood trauma reflects the psychodynamic view, and learned association reflects the behavioral view.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 36. Dawit accuses his wife of cheating on him when he is actually the one considering cheating. Dawit may be utilizing the defense mechanism called ______.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Projection attributes one's own unacceptable impulses or thoughts to another person, which is what Dawit does by accusing his wife. Displacement redirects emotion to a safer target, reaction formation expresses the opposite of a feeling, and rationalization justifies behavior with plausible excuses.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 37. If I don't care about others and the rules and regulations of a given culture, the dominant personality structure may be ______.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: The id is driven by the pleasure principle and disregards social rules and the needs of others. The superego and ego ideal embody moral standards and ideals, and the ego mediates between impulses and reality.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 38. You need to join a birthday party with your friends but you fear that you may drink too much alcohol and be exposed to various problems. This is an example of:
psy_UoG_1.explanation: The single goal of joining the party is attractive because of the friends and enjoyment, and unattractive because of the risk of drinking too much. One goal with both positive and negative aspects is an approach-avoidance conflict.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 39. Which of the following is not true about motivation?

options.text: B. Motivation is inferred from behavior
C. Motivation can be affected by different factors
D. We can observe someone's motivation directly

psy_UoG_1.explanation: Motivation is a hypothetical internal state that cannot be observed directly. It is inferred from behavior, so statement D is false. Statements A, B, and C are accurate descriptions of motivation.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 40. Suppose you are going to take another final exam for the logic course two days after your Psychology final exam. If what you studied for psychology affects your memory of logic, the kind of memory problem is _________.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Proactive interference occurs when previously learned material, here psychology, disrupts recall of newly learned material, here logic. Retroactive interference is the reverse, when new learning disrupts old memories. Primacy effect concerns serial position, and decay refers to fading over time.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 41. If you explain your motivation to study hard as resulting from your worry about getting an 'F' grade, the theory that best fits your explanation is _________
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Incentive theory explains behavior as being pulled by external goals or consequences, such as avoiding an F grade. Instinct theory relies on innate programming, arousal theory on optimal stimulation levels, and drive reduction on internal physiological tension.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 42. Alemu is studying again and again for a long time despite mastering perfect recall of the material. The memory improvement strategy employed is _________.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Overlearning is continued practice after material has been perfectly recalled, which strengthens retention and resistance to forgetting. The other strategies concern elaboration, pacing, and focus rather than repetition beyond mastery.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 43. Lemlem is always in conflict with her husband and she doesn't want to live with him but at the same time she doesn't want her children to grow up with a single parent. This is an example of:
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Lemlem faces two undesirable alternatives: staying in a conflict-ridden marriage or raising her children as a single parent. Choosing between two negatives is an avoidance-avoidance conflict.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 44. After your boss gives you a hard time at work and you come home and slam the door, kick the dog, and shout at your wife, the defense mechanism employed is _________
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Displacement redirects emotion from its real source, the boss, to safer substitute targets, the door, dog, and wife. Projection attributes one's own impulses to others, repression blocks thoughts from awareness, and sublimation channels impulses into socially acceptable activity.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 45. Which of the following is different from the others?
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Food, water, and air are physiological (biological) needs essential for survival. The need for attention is a psychological or social need, so it differs from the others.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 46. A student who justifies his cheating behavior by saying, "Everyone does it" is using the defense mechanism called _________.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Rationalization creates a plausible excuse to justify unacceptable behavior, as with 'everyone does it'. Denial refuses to acknowledge reality, repression pushes thoughts out of awareness, and projection attributes one's own impulses to others.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 47. Selam's job requires that she regularly fly to meetings around the country. She is so afraid of flying that she ends up getting fired for her refusal to travel. Selam may have a _________.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: An intense, irrational fear of one particular object or situation, here flying, is a specific phobia. Panic disorder involves recurrent unexpected panic attacks, agoraphobia involves fear of open or crowded spaces, and social phobia involves fear of social scrutiny.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 48. At different points in time, Feven has suffered from depressive and manic episodes. Feven appears to have _________.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Bipolar disorder is defined by episodes of mania and depression, and either type of episode can occur at a given time. Unipolar disorder and major depression involve only depressive episodes, and anxiety disorders are not mood-episode disorders.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 49. Every time that Meron walks out of her front door, she spends about an hour checking and rechecking the locks to make sure her home is secure. She is often late to work because of this behavior. Meron may have _________.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Repetitive checking driven by an intrusive worry about security is a compulsion, which is characteristic of obsessive-compulsive disorder. Panic disorder involves panic attacks, PTSD follows a traumatic event, and generalized anxiety disorder involves diffuse, persistent worry without ritualized behavior.

psy_UoG_1.subject: Psychology
psy_UoG_1.text: 50. As a student you are trying to memorize what was discussed in the classroom. Therefore, among the three processes involved in memory you are performing _________.
psy_UoG_1.explanation: Memorizing new material is encoding, the process of converting information into a form the memory system can store. Storage is maintaining it over time, and retrieval is accessing it later. STM is a memory store, not one of the three processes.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 1. Things most recently learned are less likely to be remembered. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: According to the recency effect, information that is learned most recently is often remembered better than information learned earlier, as it is still active in short-term memory.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 2. Motivation that is due to factors inherent to the task is called intrinsic motivation. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Intrinsic motivation refers to engaging in an activity for its own sake, because the activity itself is interesting, enjoyable, or satisfying, rather than for some separable outcome.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 3. The pioneer who contributed the concept of punishment and reinforcement was B.F. Skinner. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: B.F. Skinner is the central figure in operant conditioning and extensively studied the effects of reinforcement and punishment on behavior.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 4. A drive that is mainly learned rather than basing on biological needs is known as primary drive. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Primary drives are unlearned and biologically determined (e.g., hunger, thirst). Drives that are learned through experience are known as secondary or acquired drives.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 5. Cognitive learning theorists believe that thought processes have an important effect on learning. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Cognitive learning theories emphasize the role of mental processes such as attention, memory, and problem-solving in learning, in contrast to strictly behavioral approaches.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 6. Students learn best and retain information longer when they have meaningful practice and exercise. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Meaningful learning, where new information is connected to existing knowledge, leads to better understanding and longer retention compared to rote memorization.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 7. A student who completes learning tasks in order to earn stars on her paper is motivated by extrinsic factors. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Extrinsic motivation involves performing an activity to earn a reward or avoid punishment. In this case, the stars are an external reward.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 8. So long as pain and extreme heat or cold are inherently punishing they are considered as secondary punishers. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Stimuli that are inherently aversive and do not require learning to be punishing, such as pain or extreme temperatures, are called primary punishers.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 9. According to Maslow, a person with no job, no home, and no friends is more likely to become self-actualized. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: According to Maslow's hierarchy of needs, lower-level needs like physiological, safety (home, job security), and love/belonging (friends) must be met before a person can achieve self-actualization.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 10. Shaping is a classical conditioning procedure in which successive approximations of a desired response are reinforced. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Shaping is a procedure used in operant conditioning, not classical conditioning, where successive approximations of a target behavior are reinforced.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 11. Many psychologists believe that the internal drives work in a cycle with the external incentives to push and pull behavior respectively. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Motivation is often explained as an interaction between internal drives that 'push' an organism toward a goal and external incentives that 'pull' the organism toward them.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 12. Learning is strengthened when accompanied by an unpleasant feeling, and that learning is weakened when associated with a pleasant feeling. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Thorndike's Law of Effect states the opposite: behaviors followed by pleasant consequences are strengthened, while those followed by unpleasant consequences are weakened.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 13. One of the principles of learning is that individuals are expected to have some skills and abilities to learn in their physical and social environment. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Learning is built upon a foundation of existing skills, abilities, and biological maturation. Individuals need certain baseline capabilities to interact with and learn from their environment.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 14. In the light of the meaning of the Latin word "Movere", motivation can be defined as the internal force that moves people to do the things they do. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The statement is correct. The Latin word "movere" means "to move," and motivation is widely defined in psychology as the internal process that activates, guides, and maintains behavior over time.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 15. Social cognitive theorists believe that in human beings, observational learning can be fully understood without taking into account the thought processes of the learner. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Social cognitive theory, proposed by Albert Bandura, explicitly emphasizes the role of cognitive processes (attention, retention, motor reproduction, and motivation) in observational learning.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 16. Producing different responses to two or more similar stimuli (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Stimulus discrimination is the ability to differentiate between a conditioned stimulus and other similar stimuli, responding only to the specific conditioned stimulus.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 17. The reappearance of CR after a rest period of time (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a previously extinguished conditioned response after a period of time without exposure to the conditioned stimulus.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 18. Producing the same response to two similar but not identical stimuli (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Stimulus generalization is the tendency for the conditioned stimulus to evoke similar responses after the response has been conditioned.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 19. The diminishing of learned response when CS is not followed by UCS (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Extinction in classical conditioning is the weakening and eventual disappearance of the conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented without the unconditioned stimulus.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 20. In Pavlov's experiment the stimulus before conditioning that cannot elicit the response is ______ stimulus (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Before conditioning, the stimulus that does not naturally elicit the target response is called the neutral stimulus. In Pavlov's experiment, the bell was the neutral stimulus initially.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 21. Which one of the following is not a psychological motive? Need for: (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The need for oxygen is a fundamental biological or physiological motive, essential for survival. Achievement, affection, and belongingness are psychological or social motives.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 22. In the classical conditioning theory, the response during conditioning is ______ response (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: During the conditioning phase (acquisition), the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus. The response that occurs is primarily the unconditioned response elicited by the unconditioned stimulus. The conditioned response is the result of this pairing process.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 23. Flight and pugnacity, in approaches or theories of motivation, are examples of behaviors best explained in terms of: (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Flight (escaping) and pugnacity (fighting) are often considered innate, unlearned patterns of behavior characteristic of a species, which are defined as instincts in some motivational theories.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 24. The principle of learning which describes students can learn more from a real thing than from a substitute is (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The principle of intensity states that a vivid, dramatic, or exciting learning experience teaches more than a routine or boring one. Learning from a real object is more intense and impactful than learning from a substitute.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 25. The second step in social learning theory is (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Bandura's social learning theory outlines four steps for observational learning: 1. Attention, 2. Retention (remembering what was observed), 3. Motor reproduction, and 4. Motivation.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 26. The physiological response to natural stimulus called is ______ response (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The natural, reflexive physiological response elicited by an unconditioned stimulus (natural stimulus) is called the unconditioned response.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 27. Which theory of human motivation proposes that humans seek homeostasis and avoid state of imbalance? (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Drive-reduction theory proposes that physiological needs create an aroused tension state (a drive) that motivates an organism to satisfy the need and restore homeostasis, a balanced internal state.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 28. Unlike positive reinforcement, negative reinforcement (2021)

options.text: A. Weakens behavior by presenting unpleasant situations
B. Strengthens behavior by presenting unpleasant situations
C. Strengthens behavior by removing aversive events
D. Weakens behavior by removing aversive events

psych_HU_2021.explanation: Positive reinforcement strengthens behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus. Negative reinforcement strengthens behavior by removing or avoiding an unpleasant or aversive stimulus.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 29. Ayele has bad attitude towards physics due to bad personality of his teacher at grade 9. Later on, he develop inappropriate attitude towards all quantitative subjects. This process is: (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: This is an example of stimulus generalization, where a conditioned response (bad attitude) to a specific stimulus (physics) spreads to other similar stimuli (all quantitative subjects).

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 30. Zelalem was bitten by a dog when he was a small child. Wherever he sees that particular dog, he becomes fearful and cries. Zelalem's behavior is a good example of (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The question specifies that Zelalem becomes fearful only when he sees "that particular dog." This indicates he has learned to discriminate between the specific dog that bit him and other dogs, responding only to the original conditioned stimulus.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 31. Solving three problems to get two marks is an example of ______ schedule of reinforcement. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: In a fixed-ratio schedule, reinforcement is delivered after a specific, fixed number of responses. Here, the reinforcement (marks) is given after every three problems solved.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 32. According to Maslow's hierarchy of needs, if a person's esteem needs have been satisfied, then it is safe to assume that all of the following needs have also been satisfied except: (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Maslow's hierarchy is ordered: physiological, safety, belongingness/love, esteem, self-actualization. Needs lower in the hierarchy must be met before higher needs become salient. If esteem needs are met, the lower needs (A, B, C) are assumed to be met. Self-actualization is a higher need and is not necessarily met.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 33. In classical conditioning, learning occurs through the paring of a(an): (2021)

options.text: A. Conditioned stimulus with a conditioned responses
B. Conditioned stimulus with an unconditioned response
C. Conditioned stimulus with an unconditioned stimulus
D. Unconditioned response with unconditioned stimulus

psych_HU_2021.explanation: Classical conditioning involves pairing a neutral stimulus (which becomes the conditioned stimulus) with an unconditioned stimulus that naturally elicits a response.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 34. Select the one that is true about extrinsic motivation. (2021)

options.text: A. A motivation to engage in an activity as a means to achieve an end.
B. Based on the inherent satisfaction of a task or activity.
C. Influences the behavior of a person regardless of an immediate reward.
D. It is the motivation to engage in an activity for its own sake

psych_HU_2021.explanation: Extrinsic motivation is the drive to perform a behavior to receive an external reward or avoid punishment, rather than for the inherent satisfaction of the activity itself.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 35. Which one of the following examples of reinforcement is different from others? (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Praising is an example of a positive reinforcer (a pleasant stimulus added). Intimidating, nagging, and warning are examples of aversive stimuli, which are typically associated with punishment or negative reinforcement.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 36. Which principle of classical conditioning occurs just before the occurrence of spontaneous recovery? (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a conditioned response after it has been extinguished. Therefore, extinction must occur before spontaneous recovery can happen.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 37. A good feeling called an "aha" experience is related with ______ learning. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Insight learning, as described by Wolfgang Köhler, involves a sudden realization or understanding of a problem's solution, often accompanied by an "aha!" moment.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 38. The conditioned stimulus is: (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Based on the case study, the white gown was initially a neutral stimulus that became associated with the frightening event of seeing another child being punished. It now elicits fear on its own, making it the conditioned stimulus.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 39. What is the conditioned response? (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The conditioned response is the learned reaction to the conditioned stimulus. In this case, Mekdes's fear upon seeing a person in a white gown is the conditioned response.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 40. The unconditioned stimulus is: (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The unconditioned stimulus is the event that naturally and automatically triggers a response without prior learning. Witnessing the act of punishing another child with a stick is the unconditioned stimulus that caused fear.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 41. The unconditioned response in the above case is (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The unconditioned response is the natural, unlearned reaction to the unconditioned stimulus. The fear experienced by Mekdes upon witnessing the punishment is the unconditioned response.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 42. The learning theory concerning with such situation is ______ theory (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The situation described involves the association of a neutral stimulus (white gown) with an unconditioned stimulus (seeing punishment) to elicit a conditioned response (fear). This is the fundamental process of classical conditioning. While it involves observation, the underlying mechanism of associating stimuli is classical conditioning.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 43. The proverb which says "He who is bitten by the snake fears the lizard" related with which principle of classical conditioning? (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: This proverb illustrates stimulus generalization, where a fear response conditioned to one stimulus (snake) is elicited by a similar but different stimulus (lizard).

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 44. Observational learning theory refers to ______ learning theory (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Observational learning is a key component of Social Learning Theory, pioneered by Albert Bandura, which emphasizes learning through observing others within a social context.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 45. Which theory of learning gives advice for teachers to use peers as models in their classroom? (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Observational learning (or social learning theory) suggests that individuals learn by observing and imitating models. Using peers as models in the classroom is a direct application of this theory.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 46. As latent learning to cognitive theory operant conditioning theory is to ______ theory (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Latent learning is a concept associated with cognitive learning theories (specifically Tolman). Operant conditioning is the fundamental concept of behavioral learning theories (specifically Skinner).

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 47. Any consequence of behavior that strengthens responses or behavior by providing pleasant stimulus is ______ reinforcement (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Positive reinforcement involves the presentation of a pleasant or desirable stimulus after a behavior, which increases the likelihood of that behavior occurring again.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 48. If Kayamo become more motivated to participate in the classroom because of social approval from his teachers and classmates, the stimulus that changed his level of participation is (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Social approval is a pleasant stimulus that is added as a consequence of Kayamo's participation. Since it increased his behavior, it serves as a positive reinforcer.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 49. The salivation of Pavlov's dog before conditioning is termed as: (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Before conditioning, the dog's salivation is a natural, reflexive response to the food (unconditioned stimulus). This natural response is called the unconditioned response.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 50. Girma had been addicted of smoking cigarette for long period of time. Since the last two years, he has stopped smoking. However, when he confronts people smoking cigarette he sometimes suddenly smokes. Girma's sudden smoking cigarette is best related to (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: This is an example of spontaneous recovery, where a previously extinguished behavior (smoking) reappears after a period of time when presented with conditioned cues (seeing others smoke).

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 51. Incentive approaches to motivation suggest that motivation: (2021)

options.text: A. involves requirement of some material that is essential for survival.
B. is a result of people's thoughts, beliefs, expectations, and goals.
C. is governed by biologically determined and innate patterns.
D. stems from the desire to attain external rewards.

psych_HU_2021.explanation: Incentive theories of motivation propose that behavior is motivated by the desire to obtain external rewards or incentives.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 52. Changes resulted from fatigue and adaptation cannot be considered as learning. This concept shows us that: (2021)

options.text: A. Learning is marked by behavioral or cognitive changes
B. Changes in learning are for better or worse
C. Changes in learning should be relatively permanent

psych_HU_2021.explanation: The definition of learning emphasizes that it involves a relatively permanent change in behavior or knowledge. Temporary changes due to factors like fatigue or sensory adaptation are excluded.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 53. Select the most likely situation among the given options that would satisfy the belongingness and love need, according to Abraham Maslow. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Receiving affection directly addresses the need for love and belonging in Maslow's hierarchy. Independence and prestige relate to esteem needs, protection from harm to safety needs, and sleep/rest to physiological needs.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 54. Positive reinforcement ______ the probability that a behavior will continue and negative reinforcement ______ the probability that a behavior will continue (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: By definition, reinforcement (both positive and negative) always increases the probability or likelihood that a behavior will be repeated.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 55. As Kohler is for insight theory; ______ is for ______ theory. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: This is an analogy. Wolfgang Köhler is associated with insight learning. Similarly, B.F. Skinner is the primary figure associated with operant conditioning theory.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 56. The stimulus that triggers a reflex is known as the ______, and the reflexive response is known as the ______. The new environmental stimulus used to elicit a reflex is known as the ______ and the learned response to the new environmental stimulus is termed the ______. (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The correct sequence in classical conditioning terms is: Unconditioned Stimulus (UCS) triggers the Unconditioned Response (UCR). The new stimulus is the Conditioned Stimulus (CS), and the learned response to it is the Conditioned Response (CR).

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 57. When a person seeks to escape two unpleasant alternatives but cannot directly escape one without encountering the other, he is confronted with: (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: An avoidance-avoidance conflict occurs when a person must choose between two undesirable or unpleasant alternatives.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 58. Changes resulted from growth and maturation cannot be considered as learning. This concept implies that: (2021)

options.text: A. Learning is marked by behavioral or cognitive changes
C. Changes in learning are for better or worse

psych_HU_2021.explanation: Learning is defined as a change in behavior or knowledge due to experience or practice, distinguishing it from changes caused by biological maturation or growth.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 59. A young man wants to get married to the girl whom he loves and at the same time he wants to complete an important course in order to get a good job which is essential to start a new life. What type of conflict is he facing? (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: The young man is facing a choice between two desirable alternatives (marrying the girl he loves and completing an important course), which is characteristic of an approach-approach conflict.

psych_HU_2021.subject: Psychology
psych_HU_2021.text: 60. When you apply one of the following concepts, you start by reinforcing a tendency in the right direction. Then, you gradually require responses that are more and more similar to the final desired response. The above procedure applies to: (2021)
psych_HU_2021.explanation: Shaping is an operant conditioning procedure in which reinforcers guide behavior toward closer and closer approximations of the desired behavior.
